ledger.note: c. 1787: the Dutch land at Mempawah and fight its Panembahan. 'Not long after the Dutch landed in Mempawah in about 1787, there was a battle against the troops of Mempawah led by Panembahan Adiwijaya'; 'Syarif Kasim Alkadrie, son of Syarif Abdurrahman Alkadrie, was persuaded by the Dutch to join in the attack on Mempawah.' Adiwijaya 'finally withdrew to Karangan in Mempawah to arrange a counterattack': Karangan is the zone held against the Dutch-installed ruler (to his death in 1790, next events). The year is the page's 'about 1787'.

ledger.note: 27 August 1787: the Dutch install their candidate. 'The appointment of Syarif Kasim Alkadrie as Panembahan was enshrined in the agreement dated 27 August 1787'; 'the Dutch appointed Syarif Kasim Alkadrie as the ruler of Mempawah with the title Panembahan Mempawah.' Syarif Kasim is a son of Pontianak's sultan, who 'did not approve of the appointment'. The ruler list gives Syarif Kasim 1787-1808 and his brother Syarif Husein 1808-1820, so Mempawah is the Dutch's client for 33 years. The page says 'the Dutch', never the VOC, and quotes no terms; the counterpart is the Dutch Republic (the VOC's sovereign) to 1799 and the Dutch East Indies from 1800 (the two events below, dated from the Dutch East Indies page).

ledger.note: c. 1820: the Dutch-backed rule ends. 'When the Dutch were finally expelled from Mempawah, Gusti Jati was crowned the Sultan of Mempawah'; 'Sultan Muhammad Zainal Abidin's counterattack paid off, the Pontianak Sultanate's army was defeated.' The ruler list gives Syarif Husein 1808-1820 and Gusti Jati (Sultan Muhammad Zainal Abidin) 1820-1831; the page puts the coronation at about 1820 and gives no year for the expulsion. Independence is restored for 1820-1831 and lost again in the Dutch intervention of 1831 (dissolve). The reviewer's fix ended the vassalage at 1831; the page's expulsion and coronation sentences end it here.

ledger.note: 1831: Dutch intervention ends Mempawah's restored independence. 'In 1831, Mempawah weakened due to Dutch intervention... every succession of Mempawah has become a political game orchestrated by the Dutch.' Independence was lost twice: in 1787 (the Dutch-installed Panembahan; vassal_start 27 August 1787, 'enshrined' in the agreement) and, after the restoration of about 1820, in 1831, which is where the state ends; the last sultan was taken by the Japanese in 1944.

The page does not name the VOC. It dates the landing 'about 1787' and the agreement 27 August 1787; Adiwijaya's death is 1790 in the narrative, 1787 in the ruler list.

wars.name: Mempawah-Pontianak dispute
wars.outcome: 'Around 1794, the dispute between Mempawah and the Pontianak Sultanate grew worse'; 'the war flared up again in which the Pontianak Sultanate was assisted by the Chinese in Pontianak'; 'because the Pontianak Sultanate was fully supported by the Dutch, Mempawah was defeated in the war.' The page records no change of land: Syarif Kasim stays Panembahan to 1808.
wars.note: Pontianak was founded on 23 October 1771 by Syarif Abdurrahman Alkadrie (Pontianak Sultanate page, which says his first marriage was to a princess of the Mempawah Kingdom and that his father was a cleric from Mempawah, and does not say the site was Mempawah's); Cliopatria's Pontianak row (1772-1827) neighbours Mempawah.

wars.outcome: Mempawah's victory: 'Sultan Muhammad Zainal Abidin's counterattack paid off, the Pontianak Sultanate's army was defeated', and 'When the Dutch were finally expelled from Mempawah, Gusti Jati was crowned the Sultan of Mempawah' (ruler list 1820-1831).

notes: Two pages were opened (budget 1-2); the second, on Pontianak, gave no land change for Mempawah. Cliopatria starts the row in 1619 and ends it in 1827; the page's earliest dated sentence is c. 1610 (Raja Kudung) and its end is 1944, so the dossier runs 1610-1831 (1831 is the page's Dutch intervention), with a new keyframe for 1828-1831. The 'found' at 1610 is the page's 'around 1610' (confidence 2, raised by the reviewer): the infobox gives 'Established: 1740', which this dossier treats as a change of ruling house (rename). Before 1740 the page implies a link to the Matan Sultanate (the sultanate-of-sukadana dossier), without saying what; Landak, Banjar, Siak and Sambas are not mentioned. Capital coordinates are approximate. The sultans reigned under Dutch control until the Japanese took Sultan Thaufik in 1944; the Dutch East Indies dossier may want a dependency tint 1831-1944. The Mempawah gazetteer name is missing (only Pontianak is a place). Reviewer-fix pass (se-02-g, 2026-10-19): the Dutch intervention of 1787 is now in the ledger (contest_start about 1787 and vassal_start 27 August 1787 against dutch-republic, contest_end 1790; vassal_end 1799 and vassal_start 1800 for the split to dutch-east-indies; vassal_end about 1820) and in the wars (Dutch intervention 1787-1790, the 1794 war's outcome corrected to 'Mempawah was defeated', the 1808-1820 resistance). Independence ends twice: in 1787 (the Dutch-installed Panembahan Syarif Kasim, a Pontianak prince; Adiwijaya driven to Karangan) and, after the restoration of about 1820 ('the Dutch were finally expelled', Gusti Jati crowned), in 1831; the dossier ends at 1831. Disagreement with the reviewer's fix: it ends the vassalage at 1831; the page's expulsion and coronation sentences (and the ruler list, Gusti Jati 1820-1831) end it about 1820. It also names the war 'Dutch-Pontianak'; the page has the Pontianak sultan disapproving of the appointment. Matan link: the page says Opu Daeng Menambun came to Borneo at the request of Matan's Sultan Muhammad Zainuddin to reclaim the Matan throne; Landak is not on the Mempawah page, and the Pontianak page mentions the Landak River only as a place; neither page says how Mempawah stood to Matan or Landak before 1740 (page silent). The Karangan circle (20 km) is a guess; the gazetteer lacks Karangan. The Dutch East Indies page was a third page (budget 1-2) opened only to date the VOC's end.
